evals.prompt: Design a modular monolith for a new item analytics service. Define bounded contexts, data ownership per module, async event bus for cross-module communication, and a migration path to microservices if needed later.
evals.expected_output: Modules: ItemCore, Analytics, Reporting, Notification. Each owns its DB tables (no shared tables). Communication: sync within module, async across modules via in-process event bus (later replaceable with SQS). Migration path: each module extractable as microservice by swapping event bus impl from in-process to SQS. Keep API stable. Hexagonal: port/adapter so DB/queue implementations swappable. NEVER share tables across modules. NEVER design microservices from day 1 without proven need.

evals.prompt: Write an ADR for choosing between REST and gRPC for inter-service communication in the items ecosystem. Context: 8 Go services, need both sync (request-response) and async (event streaming) patterns.
evals.expected_output: ADR: Decision = REST (OpenAPI) for external/partner APIs, gRPC for internal service-to-service. Rationale: gRPC better performance (protobuf binary, 7-10x faster than JSON), native streaming, strong typing. REST stays for public APIs (tooling, browser compatibility). Consequences: services expose both REST + gRPC via KrakenD gateway. Complexity increased (2 protocols). NEVER choose single protocol for all use cases. NEVER skip streaming consideration.

evals.prompt: Review this architecture proposal: a item processing system with 6 microservices sharing a single PostgreSQL database. Each service has its own schema but queries across schemas freely. Identify violations and propose a fix.
evals.expected_output: Violations: Shared Database anti-pattern - database-per-service principle violated. Cross-schema queries create tight coupling (schema A change breaks schema B). Fix: migrate to database per service. Use API calls (not direct DB queries) for cross-service data access. Eventual consistency via events for data synchronization. Temporary: add PGBouncer in transaction mode for schema isolation. NEVER share databases between services. NEVER allow cross-schema queries.
